headline: State Minister Ishraque Hossain resigns after firearm controversy
summary: The Minister for Liberation War Affairs stepped down following a viral video showing him brandishing a pistol during an unauthorized anti-drug raid in Gendaria.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has resigned from his post following a controversy involving the brandishing of a firearm during a raid in his Dhaka constituency.
A viral video showed the minister pointing a pistol at people attempting to flee during a 'drug drive' in Gendaria, sparking widespread criticism on social media.
Ishraque claimed he drew the weapon for self-protection and that the raid was a coordinated effort with law enforcement, but Dhaka Metropolitan Police officials denied being part of the operation.
The incident has raised serious legal questions, as Members of Parliament do not have the constitutional authority to enforce the law or lead raids on citizens.
While reports suggested the prime minister ordered the resignation, Ishraque stated at a press conference that he stepped down voluntarily to focus on his constituency.
The resignation follows a pattern of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government removing party leaders who attract significant social media backlash, similar to the case of MP Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti.
Ishraque, the son of former Dhaka mayor Sadeque Hossain Khoka, has announced a stepped-up campaign against drug users in the area and is expected to pursue a run for mayor.
caption:
A State Minister brandishing a pistol during a 'drug raid' leads to his resignation. Was this a law enforcement operation or a political stunt?

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has resigned from his post following a controversy involving the brandishing of a firearm during a raid in his Dhaka constituency.

A viral video showed the minister pointing a pistol at people attempting to flee during a 'drug drive' in Gendaria, sparking widespread criticism on social media.

Ishraque claimed he drew the weapon for self-protection and that the raid was a coordinated effort with law enforcement, but Dhaka Metropolitan Police officials denied being part of the operation.

The incident has raised serious legal questions, as Members of Parliament do not have the constitutional authority to enforce the law or lead raids on citizens.

While reports suggested the prime minister ordered the resignation, Ishraque stated at a press conference that he stepped down voluntarily to focus on his constituency.

The resignation follows a pattern of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government removing party leaders who attract significant social media backlash, similar to the case of MP Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti.

Ishraque, the son of former Dhaka mayor Sadeque Hossain Khoka, has announced a stepped-up campaign against drug users in the area and is expected to pursue a run for mayor.

headline: 30-day ban for Ronaldo over national team camp exit
summary: The Portuguese FA has suspended the 41-year-old forward and imposed a fine following a rift with coach Jorge Jesus.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese FA after leaving the national team camp. He was also fined 255 euros ($285.83) by the federation's disciplinary council.
The incident occurred in Copenhagen before a Nations League match against Denmark. Ronaldo left the base after a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus regarding his role in the squad.
Ronaldo had accused the coach of breaking his word twice about his playing role after remaining an unused substitute during a match against Norway.
Coach Jorge Jesus denied making any such agreement but indicated that the door remains open for Ronaldo's return following Portugal's 2-1 victory.
The disciplinary council found that Ronaldo intentionally committed an offence under Article 160(1) of the federation's disciplinary regulations.
Ronaldo later apologised for leaving his teammates and failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match, stating he remains available for selection after his punishment.
Portuguese FA president Pedro Proenca stated that everyone within the federation wants Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter is resolved.
caption:
Cristiano Ronaldo suspended for 30 days! The Portuguese FA takes action after the star forward walked out of the national camp.

Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese FA after leaving the national team camp. He was also fined 255 euros ($285.83) by the federation's disciplinary council.

The incident occurred in Copenhagen before a Nations League match against Denmark. Ronaldo left the base after a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus regarding his role in the squad.

Ronaldo had accused the coach of breaking his word twice about his playing role after remaining an unused substitute during a match against Norway.

Coach Jorge Jesus denied making any such agreement but indicated that the door remains open for Ronaldo's return following Portugal's 2-1 victory.

The disciplinary council found that Ronaldo intentionally committed an offence under Article 160(1) of the federation's disciplinary regulations.

Ronaldo later apologised for leaving his teammates and failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match, stating he remains available for selection after his punishment.

Portuguese FA president Pedro Proenca stated that everyone within the federation wants Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter is resolved.
